Voyager Out-of-Distribution Generalization Campaign · 39 Models × 29 Datasets · 1,131 Cells · 11,884 Runs

Cross-Domain Generalization Matrix: 39 SPD Architectures Across 29 Benchmarks

Most Riemannian deep learning papers evaluate on 1 to 3 datasets under author-selected preprocessing, channel subsets, or epoch-peeking scripts. To separate architectural mechanisms from dataset-specific tuning, we executed a full 39-model × 29-dataset factorial grid (1,131 model-dataset cells, 11,884 subject/fold/seed evaluations) on SDSC Voyager. Every run uses 100% native EEG/fMRI channels (up to 128 EEG channels on Schirrmeister2017 and 200 Craddock ROIs on ABIDE), all available recordings, full trial windows, and strict validation-split (85% train / 15% val) checkpoint selection with zero test-set access during training.

THREE EMPIRICAL LAWS OF SPD GENERALIZATION What Transfers Across 29 Datasets When Preprocessing and Evaluation Are Held Constant
1 · SPATIOTEMPORAL STEMS & BATCHNORM BEAT RAW MATRIX DEPTH Top 5 Sweep

Models combining a learned temporal-spatial filterbank stem with Riemannian Batch Normalization occupy all five top positions across the 29 datasets: #01 ARMAGNAC-GAH (mean rank 11.17, 66.42%), #02 GBWBN (11.24, 66.32%), #03 ARMAGNAC-Harmonic (11.28, 66.49%), #04 SPDNetBN (12.03, 65.98%), and #05 ARMAGNAC-Arithmetic (12.14, 66.09%). Paired stem ablations confirm that prepending a +TSM filterbank stem lifts raw matrix models by +20 to +29 global ranks: SPDNet (#33, 61.44%) → SPDNetBN (#04, 65.98%), CorNet (#39, 57.81%) → CorNet-OLM (#19, 64.10%), and ALEM (#38, 59.59%) → SPDResNet-ALEM (#13, 64.00%).

2 · PARAMETER-FREE TOKEN MIXING BEATS MANIFOLD ATTENTION #07 SPDMetaFormer

Among standalone architectures without Riemannian BatchNorm, #06 EEGSPDNet (rank 14.86, 64.03%) and #07 SPDMetaFormer (rank 15.10, 64.57%, 6 #1 dataset wins) lead the field. SPDMetaFormer replaces Q/K/VQ/K/VQ/K/V manifold self-attention with parameter-free multi-scale pooling (k=3,5,7), yet outranks every parameterized attention model across the 29 datasets: #09 GBWAtt (15.48), #10 MAtt (16.66), #16 GyroAtt (18.59), #22 CorAtt (20.69), #24 STaRNet (20.76), and #37 SPDTransNet (29.24). On small-sample EEG sessions, learned geodesic attention weights overfit session noise rather than extracting invariant cross-session structure.

3 · DOMAIN SPECIALIZATION ACROSS BCI, CLINICAL & SPD MATRICES 3 Regimes

No single inductive bias wins every modality: (a) 15 BCI Motor/SSVEP Datasets: ARMAGNAC-Harmonic leads at 64.62%, followed by ARMAGNAC-GAH (64.12%), GBWBN (63.97%), and RHOP (63.96%), where inverse-eigenvalue harmonic weighting suppresses high-amplitude artifact bursts. (b) 10 Clinical, Sleep, ERP & fMRI Datasets: Green ranks #1 at 68.16% ahead of SPDNetBN (67.37%) and GBWBN (66.98%), because narrowband Gabor wavelets and log-diagonal power capture spectral slowing and ERP energy. (c) 4 Native SPD Matrix Benchmarks: ARMAGNAC-GAH leads at 73.95% ahead of GBWBN (73.44%) and SPDNetBN (73.28%).

JEAN-RÉMI KING CLAIM LADDER & PARETO FRONTIER Manifold Dimension d∈[2,400]d \in [2, 400]d∈[2,400] · Parameter Growth 22ch→128ch22\text{ch} \to 128\text{ch}22ch→128ch 2. Manifold Matrix Size Scaling, Parameter Complexity Pareto Frontier & Peeking Stability

To test how Riemannian architectures scale with sensor density ddd and parameter count, we stratified all 29 datasets into four covariance dimension regimes (d∈[2,19]d \in [2, 19]d∈[2,19], [20,32][20, 32][20,32], [56,64][56, 64][56,64], and [93,400][93, 400][93,400]) and measured exact parameter growth from canonical 22 ch22\text{ ch}22 ch to high-density 128 ch128\text{ ch}128 ch.

CLAIM 1D-1 · LOW-CHANNEL REGIME (d≤19d \le 19d≤19)7 Datasets

To test whether scale-invariant correlation projection preserves discriminative power on sparse sensor montages, we compared all 6 families on the 7 low-dimensional datasets (d∈[2,19]d \in [2, 19]d∈[2,19], tangent dimension 3–1903\text{--}1903–190). Correlation models drop to 56.88% (-5.25% below Riemannian BatchNorm at 62.13%), confirming that projecting P↦Δ(P)−1/2PΔ(P)−1/2P \mapsto \Delta(P)^{-1/2}P\Delta(P)^{-1/2}P↦Δ(P)−1/2PΔ(P)−1/2 discards up to half of the degrees of freedom when diagonal log-variance carries the primary ERD/ERS signal.

CLAIM 1D-2 · HIGH-DENSITY EEG (d∈[56,64]d \in [56, 64]d∈[56,64])11 Datasets

To determine when spatial filterbanks outperform metric normalization, we evaluated the 11 high-density cohorts (56–6456\text{--}6456–64 channels, tangent dimension 1,596–2,0801,596\text{--}2,0801,596–2,080). Foundational spatiotemporal filterbanks (TSMNet, EEGSPDNet, Green, TensorCSPNet) rise to #1 across all families at 64.45% (ahead of BatchNorm at 63.61%), suggesting that dense 60+ electrode montages provide the spatial resolution needed to isolate focal cortical sources prior to covariance pooling.

COHORT A · 15 BCI BENCHMARKS Motor Imagery, SSVEP, P300/ERN & Mental Workload 2. Motor-Imagery, ERP & SSVEP BCI Generalization Matrix (15 Datasets × 39 Models, Mean ± SD %)

Evaluated at 100% native channel dimensionality (up to 128×128 on Schirrmeister2017, 64×64 on Cho2017, PhysionetMI, and MAMEM2, 62×62 on Lee2019-MI, Stieger2021, and Hinss2021, and 60×60 on Weibo2014). Geodesic and harmonic batch normalization paired with spatiotemporal conv stems (ARMAGNAC-Harmonic 64.62%, ARMAGNAC-GAH 64.12%, GBWBN 63.97%) and high-order Lovrić pooling (RHOP 63.96%) lead across the 15 cohorts, while parameter-free SPDMetaFormer (62.85%) and channel-specific filterbank EEGSPDNet (62.72%) lead all standalone end-to-end models.

COHORT B · 10 CLINICAL, SLEEP, AFFECTIVE & FMRI BENCHMARKS Pathology, Sleep Staging, Oddball ERP, Emotion & Connectomes 3. Clinical, Sleep, Resting-State, ERP, Affective & fMRI Connectivity Matrix (10 Datasets × 39 Models, Mean ± SD %)

Spans clinical neurology (TUAB, TUEV), polysomnography sleep staging (Sleep-EDFX, MASS-SS3), resting-state alpha/beta oscillatory topography (LEMON 61 ch), auditory oddball ERP (TDBRAIN 26 ch), affective EEG (SEED 62 ch, DEAP 32 ch), and whole-brain resting-state fMRI functional connectivity (ABIDE 200×200 Craddock ROI, ADHD-200 190×190 ROI). Learnable Gabor wavelets in Green achieve the highest domain mean (68.16%), closely followed by SPDResNet-ALEM (68.13%), GBWAtt (67.63%), and SPDNetBN (67.37%).

Evaluated across 5 random seeds (1024..1028) with held-out validation checkpoint selection on spd-bench. On high-dimensional SPD manifolds where no temporal EEG waveform exists, Riemannian batch normalization and gyrovector layers dominate: ARMAGNAC-GAH leads overall (73.95% mean across the 4 datasets, 71.75% on 117-class HDM05), followed by GBWBN (73.44%), SPDNetBN (73.28%), GyroSPD (73.14%), and LieBN-AIM (73.05%).
